title: Hot-swap a failed drive sled in a rack without disturbing healthy bays
context: Storage servers hold their drives in hot-swappable sleds. Replacing a failed one means holding its latch down while drawing the sled out, without disturbing the healthy sleds beside it, putting the failed sled aside, and sliding in the spare whose key matches the bay until the bay lamp turns green. The task asks a dual-arm robot to do this in a tight three-bay rack.
instruction: One bay has a red lamp. Replace its drive sled with the spare that matches the bay's key tab, and put the removed sled on the discard pad, without moving the other two sleds.
setup: All positions are cm from the midpoint between arm bases (x forward, y left); table top is z = 0 (0.7475 m in the simulator world frame). Server rack: 16.0 x 40.0 x 6.0 cm open-front aluminium chassis, 10.0 kg (ballast under the floor, rubber feet, friction 1.0, not bolted), front face at x = 33.0 cm, centre (41.0, 0.0); 1.0 cm floor, 0.9 cm back, 0.8 cm top plate starting 2.5 cm behind the front face. Three bay slots 10.4 cm wide at y = +12.0, 0.0, -12.0 cm (pitch 12.0 cm, 1.2 cm clearance each side of an 8.0 cm sled, bay floor 1.0 cm above the table). Three aluminium sleds, 15.0 x 8.0 x 2.5 cm, 0.050 kg, friction 1.5, seated with their centre at x = 40.5 cm, each with a 3.0 x 4.5 x 3.0 cm black front handle. Latch buttons: 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.2 cm brass spring buttons (100 N/m, 8 mm stroke, pressed at >= 6.4 mm) on the top plate at x = 40.5 cm, 5.5 cm to the left of each bay's centre line. Key tabs: 2.0 x 2.0 x 0.3 cm coloured tabs on the top plate at x = 37.2 cm in front of each bay: bay 0 and bay 2 orange, bay 1 (the failed bay) blue. A spare fits a bay when its handle colour matches the bay's key tab. 2.5 cm status marker lamps on the top plate at x = 45.5 cm over each bay (bay 1 red, bays 0 and 2 green; a green marker replaces the red one when the bay is solved). Spare stand: 18.0 x 18.0 x 2.0 cm plate (4.0 kg) at (28.0, +30.0) holding a blue-handled spare at (28.0, +25.0) and an orange-handled spare at (28.0, +35.0), each a sled as above (15.0 x 8.0 x 2.5 cm, 0.050 kg, friction 1.5, long side along x, handle facing the robot), centre 7.8 cm above the table. Discard pad: 13.0 x 13.0 x 1.0 cm rubber pad (2.0 kg) at (28.0, -30.0).
scoring: Score of the current step (end-state; the score never keeps a best value). 0.25 when the failed sled has been pulled >= 6.0 cm with the latch held; 0.50 when the removed sled is resting on the discard pad now (centre within 4.0 cm of the pad centre in x and y and within 1.0 cm of resting height); 0.75 when the removed sled is on the pad and the blue spare is seated >= 95% in the failed bay now (centre within 0.8 cm of the seated x position, 1.5 cm of the bay centre line and 1.5 cm of resting height); 1.00 when, in addition, the status lamp is green (blue spare seated, latch released), both grippers are open, both arms are clear (no arm point at x >= 28.0 cm with |y| <= 25.0 cm) and still (< 5 mm/s, < 0.2 rad/s) and healthy sleds are undisturbed, held for 20 control steps (1.0 s at 20 Hz). Zero-gates, latched for the rest of the run: pulling the failed sled more than 3 mm (up to 25 mm) without the latch pressed is a forced-pull FAULT; moving any healthy sled more than 5 mm is a FAULT. The start state scores 0.0.
reset_notes: Verify all three sleds are fully seated (centre x = 40.5 cm) and the latch buttons are at rest height. Ensure bay 1's lamp is red and bays 0 and 2 are green, and that the key tab over bay 1 is blue and the others orange. Confirm the blue spare is at (28.0, +25.0) and the orange spare at (28.0, +35.0) on the stand, and the discard pad at (28.0, -30.0) is clear.
fidelity: Rigid rack, sleds, stand and pad with the masses and friction in the setup; the latch buttons are real spring sliders (100 N/m, 8 mm). In software: the latch retention (a forced pull is a fault; the sled itself slides freely), the keying (a rule on the spare's handle colour; a wrong spare can be pushed in but the lamp stays red) and the lamps. Real build: rack-mount server with spring latch pins in 25 mm rail detents and 6 mm key ribs, at a quarter of scale.
